subject: DPA execution: subprocessor attestation and signature routing plan
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finoptima.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finoptima.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA draft — subprocessor attestations and execution path

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft last week. Before we move to signature we need two things confirmed on Redwood's side:

1) A current list of subprocessors with attestations that no customer data is used for model training, and an exportable spreadsheet we can attach to our procurement record.
2) The exact signature flow you plan to use (DocuSign/AdobeSign), who signs first, and whether countersign will come from an authorized executive on your legal team or from Ops. We need to map the envelope routing to our internal procurement and legal approvers.

We also received a few redline comments from our GC — primarily around data transfer and EU SCCs — but we've paused final sign-off until the subprocessor attestation is included in the exhibit.

Can you share the attestation file and a proposed execution schedule this week? Our target is to have the DPA fully executed by Jun 8 so our procurement systems can close the PO.

Best,
Elena
Legal, FinOptima

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finoptima.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA draft — subprocessor attestations and execution path

Elena — thanks for the note and the timeline.

Quick summary / proposal:
- Attachments: attaching our current subprocessor attestations spreadsheet (subprocessor-attestation-20280529.xlsx) and the DPA with our internal redlines (DPA-redline-sofia-20280531.pdf). The spreadsheet includes an attest column for training-data use; all entries are "no" as of 2028-05-29.
- Signature flow: we propose Redwood to Initiate in DocuSign (customer signs first). Routing:
  1) FinOptima Legal (Elena) signs
  2) FinOptima Procurement (procurement@finoptima.com) acknowledges / signs if required
  3) Redwood Legal (Karthik) receives notification and signs as countersign
  4) Final copy archived to both parties' DocuSign envelopes and Google Drive link shared
- Signatory authority: Karthik is authorized to countersign all DPAs under $500k; for higher value deals we escalate to VP Legal. I've attached a signature-authority-matrix.csv for reference.
- Timeline: we can create the DocuSign envelope today and aim for countersign by Jun 3 end of day if FinOptima signs by Jun 2.

Questions for you:
- Do you require a separate exhibit file embedded in the DocuSign envelope (preferred) or is a Drive link acceptable to attach to the procurement record?
- Any specific fields/metadata your procurement system needs populated in the envelope (PO number, contract id)?

I'll proceed to prepare the envelope today and will loop Karthik/Neha for the countersign step.

Thanks,
Sofia
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finoptima.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 12:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA draft — subprocessor attestations and execution path

Elena / Sofia — quick confirmation from legal ops side:
- Countersign OK as proposed. I will countersign from the DocuSign console; no further manual notarization needed.
- We prefer the exhibit embedded in the envelope (makes audit trail cleaner). Please include the subprocessor-attestation spreadsheet as an embedded attachment (PDF or XLSX).
- If FinOptima can include PO# in the "Payment/PO" envelope field that would make downstream matching simpler.

I'll be on standby for the envelope notification; Neha will help confirm the redline snapshot matches the final attached exhibit before countersign.

—Karthik
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finoptima.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finoptima.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 15:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA draft — subprocessor attestations and execution path

Sofia / Karthik — thanks for the clarity. Procurement is fine with the exhibit embedded. We'll add PO# FIN-98765 in the envelope metadata.

Two small asks before we sign:
- Can you add a short clause to the exhibit cover sheet that the attestation is "current as of the signature date"? That helps our audit team.
- Please confirm whether AdobeSign is acceptable in case DocuSign presents regional latency; our procurement endpoint restricts some third-party redirects.

If those are OK we'll expect the envelope link and will route internally for signature (target still Jun 2).

Regards,
Elena

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finoptima.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finoptima.com>

Elena — all set. Summary of actions completed: 
- Embedded attestation file in the DocuSign envelope and added the phrase "Attestation current as of signature date" to the exhibit cover page (see attached PDF in the envelope).
- Created envelope in DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC-12345 (access restricted to FinOptima + Redwood signatories).
- PO# FIN-98765 populated in the envelope metadata.
- AdobeSign fallback: Yes — we will create an AdobeSign parallel envelope if you cannot access DocuSign due to routing restrictions. Please advise within 24 hours if we should switch.

Karthik / Neha: once FinOptima completes step 1 we will wait for notification and then countersign (expected same day). Neha, please snapshot the final agreed redline before you click countersign.

Thanks everyone — I will follow up with the envelope status once FinOptima begins signing.

Sofia
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
